latin: Nec rhumīī pōcillum<sup>1</sup> nec hispānicam accipere vīs?
Sed age, forsitan<sup>2</sup> tibi sit in vōtīs aliud quid<sup>3</sup>, aiēbat magistrātus cuidam condemnātō, quīnque minūtīs ante supplicium ejus.
Nempe, Domne Jūdex<sup>4</sup>, is respondit, ā pueritiā tōtā semper mente<sup>5</sup> linguam hebraicam discere optāvī!
Diārium<sup>6</sup> cujusdam cīvitātis, cum<sup>7</sup> hunc mātrimōniālem libellum pūblicāvisset:
«Villicī<sup>8</sup> fīlia, 30 annōs nāta, fōrmōsō<sup>9</sup> corpore, dulcissimā nātūrā, multa spērāns, recentissimamque vīllam possidēns<sup>10</sup>, adulēscentī nūbere cupit, etc.»
Rescrīpsit quīdam: «Spērātōrum indicem<sup>11</sup> mitte, vīllaeque imāginem<sup>12</sup> photographicam».
Autoraedārius quīdam, cum, albīs ālīs ōrnātus, Sānctum Petrum adīret<sup>13</sup>, ā paradīsī jānitōre quidnam sibi accidisset<sup>14</sup> interrogātus, ita respondit:
Quid acciderit nōn intellegō: paucās vix<sup>15</sup> abhinc minūtās cum uxōre autoraedam beātus regēbam<sup>16</sup>...
«Sī gubernāculum<sup>17</sup> mihi commodāre velīs, angelus vērē sīs!»
latinAccented: Nec rhumī́ī pōcíllum<sup>1</sup> nec hispā́nicam accípere vīs?
Sed age, fórsitan<sup>2</sup> tibi sit in vōtīs áliud quid<sup>3</sup>, aiḗbat magistrā́tus cúidam condemnā́tō, quīnque minū́tīs ante supplícium ejus.
Nempe, Domne Jūdex<sup>4</sup>, is respóndit, ā puerítiā tōtā semper mente<sup>5</sup> linguam hebráicam díscere optā́vī!
Diā́rium<sup>6</sup> cujúsdam cīvitā́tis, cum<sup>7</sup> hunc mātrimōniā́lem libéllum pūblicāvísset:
«Víllicī<sup>8</sup> fī́lia, 30 annōs nāta, fōrmṓsō<sup>9</sup> córpore, dulcíssimā nātū́rā, multa spērāns, recentissimámque vīllam póssidēns<sup>10</sup>, adulēscéntī nū́bere cupit, etc.»
Rescrī́psit quīdam: «Spērātṓrum índicem<sup>11</sup> mitte, vīlláeque imā́ginem<sup>12</sup> photográphicam».
Autoraedā́rius quīdam, cum, albīs ālīs ōrnā́tus, Sānctum Petrum adī́ret<sup>13</sup>, ā paradī́sī jānitṓre quidnam sibi accidísset<sup>14</sup> interrogā́tus, ita respóndit:
Quid accíderit nōn intéllegō: paucās vix<sup>15</sup> abhinc minū́tās cum uxṓre autoráedam beā́tus regḗbam<sup>16</sup>...
«Sī gubernā́culum<sup>17</sup> mihi commodā́re velīs, ángelus vērē sīs!»
english: You don't want [to take] a little glass of rum or a cigarette?
But come, perhaps [you have something] else [to ask for] (be to you in your wishes), said the magistrate to a condemned man, five minutes before his execution.
Certainly, Your Honour (Judge), the latter replied, since my childhood I have always wished with all my heart to learn Hebrew!
As a [local] newspaper (of a certain town) had published this marriage advertisement:

«Farmer's daughter, 30 years old (born), [physically attractive] (with a beautiful body), very affectionate nature, [great] expectations (hoping much), owning an ultra-modern farm, wishes to marry young man, etc.»
Someone replied: «[Send] (sent) [details of] the expectations and [a photograph] of the farm (photographic image)».

A motorist, as, adorned with white wings, he [presented himself to] Saint Peter (approached), [and the] gatekeeper of paradise [asked him what could have happened to him] (by the gatekeeper what to himself had happened questioned), replied thus:
I don't understand what happened (subj. perfect): barely a few minutes ago, I was driving [happily] (happy) [my] car with [my] wife...
I only remember her last words:
«If you were willing to lend me the wheel, you would be a real angel.»

footnotes: Pocillum, -i, n., small glass, diminutive of poculum.

Forsitan (or forsan + subj.), perhaps = fors sit an (fors, fortis, f., chance). An, conj., is it that?, is construed in general with utrum; e.g.: nescio utrum loqui an silere debeam, I don't know if I should (ought to) speak or be silent.
Aliquis, aliqua, aliquid, something; aliusquis, aliaquae, aliudquid, something else.
Tota... mente, with all one's mind (heart); another example of separation of the epithet and its antecedent.
Diarium, -ii, n., comes from dies, -ei, m. or f., the day. We have already seen diurnarius, the journalist.

Cum, conj., in the sense of then, as, is construed with the subjunctive (here p.q.p.) if it is a past fact having as its effect a cause action expressed by the main verb: if the newspaper had not published the advertisement, the quidam of sentence 6 would not have replied (rescripsit).
Villa, -ae, f., farm; villicus, -i, m., the farmer.
Formosus, -a, -um, beautiful as to form (forma, -ae, beauty, form).
Index, -icis, m., sign, index; here, indication (list).
Again cum with the imperfect subjunctive (adiret).

Quidnam sibi accidisset: INDIRECT QUESTION (here with subj. p.q.p.). The direct question would be (interrogatus est): quidnam tibi accidit? (ind. pft). The same word (here quidnam, what then) can just as well introduce the direct question as the indirect question. There are three impersonal verbs to say: it happens (that): accidit, an unforeseen event occurs (sometimes unfortunate); cf. casus, -us, m., chance, accident; evenit, any event occurs; contingit, a foreseen (or happy) event occurs. Note that these verbs, generally used in the impersonal form, can have a subject, if it corresponds to the 3rd person (here quid).
Vix, adv., hardly. Abhinc = ab + hinc, from here, from there.
Rego, -is, -ere, rexi, rectum; derivative: dirigere (same conjugation).
Gubernaculum, -i, n., rudder (here, steering wheel); one could also have said: manubrium, -i, n., handle, handlebar (of a bicycle).
comments: Maecenas, -atis, Maecenas; rich contemporary of Augustus and generous protector of letters and the arts. — Protegere = pro + tegere; we have already seen tegmen (L. 48, N. 3).

latin: Vīvat et rēs pūblica, et quī illam regit! (bis)
latinAccented: Vīvat et rēs pū́blica, et quī illam regit! (bis)
english: Long live all the girls, playful and beautiful!
Long live the Republic too, and he who governs it!
